[FACT] User is looking for BBQ recipe ideas, specifically for grilled chicken breasts.  
[FACT] User has been watching BBQ YouTube channels, specifically "Smoky's BBQ" and "Grill Master 3000."  
[PREFERENCE] User is excited to try out new techniques for BBQ.  
[PREFERENCE] User is interested in marinades or seasonings that would pair well with a sweet and smoky flavor profile.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Sweet & Smoky BBQ Marinade: Mix together 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, 1 teaspoon garlic powder, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Honey Mustard BBQ Marinade: Combine 1/2 cup honey, 1/4 cup Dijon mustard, 2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Molasses & Bourbon Marinade: Whisk together 1/2 cup molasses, 1/4 cup bourbon whiskey, 2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Smoky Sweet Rub: Mix together 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 2 tablespoons smoked paprika, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 tablespoon onion powder, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Sweet Heat Rub: Combine 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 1 tablespoon chili powder, 1 tablespoon ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested a Grill Master's Magic Dust: Blend 2 tablespoons brown sugar, 1 tablespoon smoked paprika, 1 tablespoon garlic powder, 1 tablespoon onion powder, 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, and 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended marinating chicken breasts for at least 2 hours or overnight for maximum flavor penetration.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised to preheat the grill to medium-high heat (around 375°F) for a nice sear and caramelization.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested not pressing down on the chicken breasts while grilling to prevent juices from being squeezed out.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended letting the chicken rest for 5-10 minutes before slicing and serving to allow juices to redistribute.
